standard.title: Initiate exchanges and respond about self and environment
standard.description: initiate exchanges and respond to modelled questions about self, others, and classroom environment, using formulaic expressions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can recognise and respond to modelled greetings, instructions and routines, and produce personal introductions using modelled sentence structures (AC9LS2C01). They respond to questions but have not yet initiated exchanges independently or used a range of interrogatives.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students initiate exchanges and respond to questions about self, others and the classroom environment using formulaic expressions and modelled structures — including routines, interests, family, location and time.

nodes.label: Initiating and responding in personal exchanges
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can initiate an exchange about themselves or others using appropriate formulaic expressions, and respond to questions about personal life, family, interests and routines.
nodes.minimum_width: Initiate at least one exchange using an appropriate greeting or question without teacher prompting; respond to at least three personal questions using modelled sentence structures.
nodes.typical_width: Use formal and informal forms of address across contexts; exchange information about family, friends and interests using simple statements and connecting words; use question-answer patterns about school and home life; describe routines using time expressions; use a range of question words.
wider: Conduct a short unrehearsed exchange with a partner — initiating, sustaining and closing without teacher scripting — using at least four different question types
Exchange information about routines across different time references and explain the pattern of a typical week
nodes.hinge_reason: Initiating exchanges — rather than only responding — is the core progression from 1-2 to 3-4. Students who can only respond cannot engage in the planning, collaborative and text comprehension tasks at this band, all of which require interactive initiation.

response_modes.reason: Initiation requires a bank of question forms and opening strategies across personal domains. Students need varied practice asking and answering across different topic areas to build the range needed for genuine initiation.

success_criteria: Initiates at least one exchange using an appropriate greeting or opening question without teacher prompting
Responds to at least three different personal questions using modelled sentence structures

nodes.label: Describing environment, features and locations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the features, characteristics and locations of things and places in the classroom environment using location language and descriptive expressions.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe the location of at least two objects using location expressions; describe at least one feature or characteristic of a place or object.
nodes.typical_width: Use a range of location expressions; describe characteristics, size and location of places and things; respond to questions about the classroom environment; use question-answer patterns about school life and surroundings.
wider: Give and follow multi-step directions to locate an object or place — demonstrating command of spatial language beyond single-object description
Describe a space outside the immediate classroom using at least four different location or descriptive expressions

response_modes.reason: Location and descriptive language develops through practice across varied physical environments and object sets. Students who only describe the immediate classroom develop narrow spatial language schemas.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Environmental description is the foundation for spatial communication across all subsequent contexts — directions, transactions, travel. Width investment here builds the spatial language repertoire that recurs through the sequence.
success_criteria: Uses at least two different location expressions correctly to describe the position of objects
Describes at least one characteristic or feature of a place or object using appropriate target language

nodes.label: Making requests and managing communication
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make and respond to requests — including requests for items, help, clarification and repetition — using modelled expressions.
nodes.minimum_width: Make at least one request and ask for at least one form of clarification or repetition using modelled target language expressions.
nodes.typical_width: Make requests for items and assistance; request permission; ask for clarification and repetition; respond to requests from others; use modelled expressions for managing communication breakdowns.
wider: List at least three strategies for managing communication difficulty in the target language — demonstrating a metacommunicative repertoire beyond a single formula
Use a metacommunicative expression spontaneously during a real communication difficulty — not only in a rehearsed scenario

response_modes.reason: Request and clarification language becomes genuinely available only when students have a bank of expressions across varied request types. Students who know only one formula are limited in real interaction contexts.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Requesting clarification independently is a high-value metacommunicative skill that enables students to manage genuine communication breakdowns. This capability matters in every subsequent interaction context.
success_criteria: Makes at least one request using appropriate target language expressions
Asks for clarification or repetition using at least one modelled metacommunicative expression
